newsitem.title: CHINA: Australian PM's China visit to boost trade links.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM's China visit to boost trade links.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard will use his forthcoming visit to China to boost trade with Beijing and further open the way for Chinese firms to list shares in Australia, an Australian diplomat said on Tuesday.
Howard, who is to visit China from March 29 to April 2, will raise political issues in talks with his Chinese hosts, but his tour would also have a heavy economic focus, the diplomat said.
"For Australia, we see our major foreign and trade policy interests in the future lying in the Asian region, and in that context, place a very high importance on China," he said.
Some 60 percent of Australia's exports were shipped to East Asia, and Canberra was eager to boost that figure, he said.
"The countries that are closest with us are the best ones to trade with, they are also the countries of the world that are growing the fastest," he said.
China is Australia's fifth largest trading partner, with two-way trade worth $6.3 billion in the year to June 30, 1996.

Howard would have in tow representatives of 18 businesses as well as officials from the Australian Stock Exchange who would hold a seminar to advise Chinese firms on how to list shares in Australia based on a 1996 agreement, the diplomat said.
"A large number of Chinese companies will be invited to the seminar and they will be given a presentation by people from the stock exchange and (Chinese regulators) on how to go about this," he said.
The business group would include firms that already had a strong presence in the Chinese market as well as companies looking to tap into new areas such as finance, he said.

Howard's visit is also intended to mend fences with Beijing and leave behind a series of rows that have included Canberra's military ties with the United States and its hosting last year of exiled Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama.
